candidate.title: Calendar interface migration to destinationCalendar[] + credentialId is not enforced; unmigrated implementers still type-check
reports: packages/types/calendar.d.ts:221 — the calendar.createevent interface signature changed to require credentialid, but no test verifies that other calendarservice implementations or mocks handle the new argument.

packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:207-229 — stripe (and paypal-webhook.ts:152-156) payment-success path builds destinationcalendar from a single calendar, so paid collective events are written only to the organizer's calendar after payment, not each host's (p1, conf 100)

packages/types/calendar.d.ts:221 — the provider-neutral credentialid selector is consumed only by google while office, lark, and basecalendarservice select element zero, so collective non-first hosts can target the first host's calendar and each provider inherits hidden selection rules.

team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has none — evt.destinationcalendar is set to null instead of [] so the push of teamdestinationcalendars no-ops, and the booking row only connects destinationcalendar[0].id so members' destination calendars are not persisted for later cancel/reschedule flows

eventmanager.ts / calendarmanager.ts — no test coverage for the type-level breaking change (destinationcalendar → destinationcalendar[]), the collective multi-host path, the credential db-fallback, or the crashing empty-array case; only a playwright snapshot value was touched

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:119 — the bookingcreated and bookingrequested fixtures (lines 119 and 373) still assert null while bookingrejected asserts [], which locks in two different "no calendar" values for the same array field (handlenewbooking returns : null, confirm.handler returns : []), so webhook consumers get a different payload type depending on the trigger and no test flags the mismatch (p2, conf 75; verbatim: destinationcalendar: null,)
